Microservices & Resilience Patterns

Learn why companies split one big program into many small services, and the small set of tools (timeouts, retries with jitter, circuit breakers, bulkheads, load shedding) that keep one sick service from taking the whole site down.

sections.before:
Level 5 - Interview-ready

You might confuse this with... rate limiting vs load shedding: a rate limiter caps each client at an agreed rate (per user or API key) and returns 429, even when the server is idle; load shedding protects the server by rejecting low-priority work when it is actually overloaded, whoever sends it, and returns 503. And timeout vs deadline: a timeout is "this one call may take 200 ms"; a deadline is "the whole user request must finish by 12:00:00.300", passed down every hop.
